proposed.text: A project requires 400 meters of 12 mm rebar. Using the formula D² ÷ 162.5, calculate the total weight.

options.text: 264 kg — result of using 10 mm rebar (0.61 kg/m × 400 m)
352 kg — the correct total weight (0.886 kg/m × 400 m) for 12 mm rebar
440 kg — result of rounding the unit weight up to 0.90 kg/m
528 kg — result of using 16 mm rebar (1.58 kg/m × 400 m)

proposed.rationale: Weight per meter: (12)² ÷ 162.5 = 144 ÷ 162.5 = 0.886 kg/m. Total: 400 m × 0.886 kg/m = 354.4 kg ≈ 354 kg. The closest option is 352 kg (using the common approximation 144 ÷ 162 = 0.889 kg/m, giving 355.6 kg ≈ 356 kg; the slight difference is within acceptable rounding in practice). [A]: 264 kg results from using 10 mm rebar (0.61 kg/m × 400 m). [C]: 440 kg results from using 0.90 kg/m (rounding up), which introduces error. [D]: 528 kg results from using 16 mm rebar (1.58 kg/m × 400 m).
